Try Materials.Ai David Willson 08.21.2026 Manufacturing Processes Time to read: 14 min Most prototyping conversations center on CNC machining and 3D printing, and for good reason: both provide parts fast, which is a real advantage for early design work. Once a metal component is headed toward production casting, however, these prototyping methods don’t fully represent the manufacturing conditions and final product. Using the same process for prototypes and production parts gives engineers a better read on the manufacturability and performance earlier in development. Casting prototypes produced using die casting, investment casting, or gravity mold casting give engineering teams production-representative material properties, geometry, and process behavior that CNC-machined or 3D-printed stand-ins cannot replicate. This article covers three of the main methods for metal prototypes and low-volume work: die casting, investment casting, and gravity (permanent mold) casting. Cast metal prototypes Why Consider Casting for Prototyping? For one-off proof-of-concept parts, CNC machining or additive manufacturing is usually the fastest path. If you’re weighing casting vs CNC machining , our comparison guide explains when each process makes the most sense. The case for casting strengthens as you move down the product design path toward final production intent, material validation, and process confirmation. Material Properties That Match Production A CNC prototype is machined from a solid metal stock—typically wrought billet, bar, or plate. A cast part solidifies from molten metal. That difference shows up in grain structure, porosity, residual stress, high-cycle fatigue life, pressure tightness, and how the part responds to heat treatment. If your structural fatigue, pressure, or regulatory tests need to reflect production conditions, build the prototype using the same casting process family as the final part. A cast prototype will provide more useful results than a machined or printed stand-in. Geometry You Can Actually Produce Casting can produce internal passages, thin walls, ribs, and complex contours that would require multiple CNC setups or wire EDM, or that simply cannot be machined. A design refined only through CNC-machine prototypes still requires redesign and decisions on draft, wall thickness, shrinkage, gating, and parting lines for production casting. Fewer Surprises at Production A cast prototype can reveal fill problems, hot spots, and distortion before production tooling is cut. Addressing these issues during prototype development reduces engineering changes later, when production tooling is complete. Cast parts have longer lead times and higher upfront costs than a single CNC-machined or printed part. But casting begins to earn its keep when volume rises, or when the production process itself needs validation. The Three Primary Metal Casting Methods for Prototyping The right choice of prototype casting method depends on production volume, alloy, geometry, tooling budget, and how closely the prototype process needs to match the eventual production process. Die casting mold Die Casting: Production-Like Parts Require a Tooling Investment Die casting injects molten metal under high pressure into a reusable steel mold. For production programs that will run high-pressure die casting (HPDC) , it is the only process that can deliver the same alloy family, fill dynamics, solidification history, and residual stress state, provided the process parameters stay comparable. Common HPDC materials include aluminum alloys such as A380, A383, A360, and ADC12 as well as zinc. These alloys generally cannot be heat treated to T6 because the high-pressure mold fill can trap gas in the molten metal, causing surface blisters during the solution phase of T6 heat treatment. If you do not yet need that production microstructure, or the design is still changing, investment casting or gravity casting will usually cost less and move faster. Wax patterns prepared for investment casting Investment Casting: Complex Geometry at Low Volume Investment casting (lost wax casting) uses a ceramic shell built around a wax pattern. The wax is burned out, and molten metal is poured into the shell. For prototypes, the wax patterns can be 3D printed , eliminating the need for hard tooling. First parts typically arrive in 1 to 3 weeks, making investment casting one of the most practical metal casting routes for low-volume work. Investment casting accommodates a broad alloy range: stainless, tool steels, aluminum, titanium, Inconel, cobalt chrome, and many specialty alloys. The surface finish of investment-cast parts is usually Ra 1.6 to 3.2 μm as-cast, with dimensional accuracy around ±0.1 to 0.25 mm on most features. Undercuts, internal passages, and thin walls are routine. One practical caveat: thin sections cool faster than thick ones in the same part, so local microstructure and mechanical properties can vary with section thickness. Test results from one section may therefore not represent another. Investment casting is best suited for small- to medium-complexity parts (aerospace and medical components) and projects with too low a volume to justify die casting (1 to 500 pieces). Cycle times are slower for investment casting than for die casting, cost per part rises at higher volumes, and critical interfaces still need CNC finishing. Investment-cast aluminum behaves differently from die-cast aluminum and is not a valid stand-in when HPDC is the intended production process. Tilt pour gravity casting Gravity/Permanent Mold Casting: Structural Aluminum at Mid-Volumes Gravity casting (permanent mold casting) pours molten metal into a reusable steel or iron mold under gravity rather than pressure. It sits between die casting and sand casting in terms of cast part quality: better surface finish and dimensional consistency than sand casting, lower tooling cost, and lower porosity than HPDC. It is a common route for the production of heat-treatable aluminum castings at moderate volumes. Using only the force (pressure) of gravity to fill a mold produces less turbulence and less trapped gas in the resulting casting than high-pressure injection. That lower porosity lets alloys such as A356 reach T6 without blistering. Tooling for gravity mold casting is simpler than that for HPDC, and is typically less expensive. Tooling lead time is in the 3 to 5 week range: less than for HPDC, but longer than it takes to get started with investment casting. Surface finish of gravity mold castings is typically Ra 2 to 6 μm, and tolerances land around ±0.2 to 0.5 mm depending on part complexity. Permanent mold casting prototypes are best for mid-complexity aluminum housings, structural parts, pressure-tight enclosures, and any project where porosity or heat treatability matters. Compared to HPDC, gravity fill castings are restricted to higher minimum wall thickness (around 3 to 4 mm for reliable fill and feeding), more limited undercut geometry options, and slower production cycle time. Other Prototype Casting Methods Worth Knowing About Sand casting has the lowest tooling cost and the most flexibility for large parts or single-piece quantities, but surface finish and dimensional accuracy lag the three primary methods. Urethane casting is another prototyping process, but not for metals. It is used to produce polyurethane parts from silicone molds, and works well for appearance-quality plastic prototypes (roughly 5 to 150 pieces) when injection mold tooling is not yet justified. How to Choose the Right Casting Method for Your Prototype No single process is the best for every set of project requirements. The decision about which one to select turns on how closely the prototype needs to match the production process, which alloy you need, how much tooling budget you have, and how many parts you expect to run. Die Casting vs Investment Casting vs Gravity Casting Factor Die Casting Investment Casting Gravity / Permanent Mold Casting Best suited for HPDC production validation Complex, low-volume metal parts Structural aluminum parts Tooling Required (prototype or production tooling) None (3D-printed wax patterns) Required Typical lead time 2–8 weeks 1–3 weeks 3–5 weeks Typical volume 50–5,000+ parts 1–500 parts 50–3,000 parts Material options Primarily aluminum-, magnesium-, and zinc-based alloys Very broad (stainless steel, titanium, aluminum alloys, tool steels, nickel alloys, and more) Primarily aluminum alloys (A356, A319, A360); Zinc, copper, and magnesium also used Heat treatable Generally not for HPDC aluminum alloys Yes Yes Typical surface finish Ra 0.8–3.2 μm as-cast Ra 1.6–6.3 μm as-cast Ra 2–6.3 μm as-cast Best prototype choice when… Production validation is the priority Design flexibility and alloy selection matter most Heat-treatable aluminum is required or HPDC tooling isn’t yet justified Design Considerations for Cast Metal Prototypes Addressing the following design considerations early helps reduce tooling revisions, improves part quality, and shortens the path to production. Die casting DFM guidance Wall Thickness Minimum wall thickness depends on the casting process. High-pressure die casting (HPDC) can typically achieve aluminum alloy wall sections of 1.5 to 2 mm . Investment casting generally supports 1 to 2 mm , depending on the alloy and geometry. Gravity casting usually requires 3 to 4 mm minimum to ensure reliable mold filling and feeding. Design to the wall thickness your strength requirements demand, then choose a casting process that can reliably produce it. Unnecessary thickness creates hot spots that cool more slowly, increasing the risk of shrinkage porosity while also extending cycle times and raising material costs. When additional stiffness is required, use ribs or gussets instead of thickening the entire wall. Draft Angles Every casting process benefits from proper mold draft angles to facilitate part or pattern removal. Die casting typically requires 1° to 3° of draft, while gravity casting generally needs 2° to 5° . Investment casting is more forgiving because the ceramic shell is destroyed after solidification, but incorporating modest draft still improves dimensional consistency and helps reduce residual stress caused by mold constraint. Post-Casting Machining Allowances Almost every cast prototype requires CNC machining on critical features such as sealing surfaces, precision bores, bearing seats, and mating interfaces. Cast in 0.5-1.5 mm of machining stock on these surfaces and clearly identify the allowance on the engineering drawing. Parting Lines, Gates, and Shrinkage Parting line and gate locations should be reviewed with your manufacturing partner before tooling begins. These decisions influence how molten metal fills the cavity, affect cosmetic appearance, and determine where porosity is most likely to occur. Design parts to their nominal dimensions and let the foundry apply the appropriate shrinkage compensation during tooling design. Typical linear shrinkage is approximately 0.5 to 0.6% for HPDC, 0.8 to 1.2% for gravity casting, and 1.0 to 1.5% for investment casting, depending on the alloy and section thickness. Shrinkage is never perfectly uniform. Thick sections cool and contract differently from thin sections, which can introduce distortion across the part. For that reason, critical interfaces should be machined to their final dimensions rather than relying on as-cast tolerances. Learn more about DFM for metal casting in our Scaling CNC to Casting Guide . How Fictiv Supports Casting for Prototyping and Low-Volume Production Fictiv supports cast metal parts from prototyping through low-volume production, with manufacturing guidance and casting-specific DFM feedback along the way. DFM feedback for casting identifies issues with draft, wall thickness, parting lines, and machining allowances while they’re still inexpensive to correct. Need cast metal prototypes? Get a quote for die casting, investment casting, and gravity casting options for prototype builds through Fictiv’s manufacturing network. Talk to a Fictiv expert about your project, or upload your parts to start a free quote. Talk to an Expert Upload Parts & Get a Free Quote FAQs About Prototyping With Casting What’s the difference between die casting and investment casting for prototypes? Die casting injects molten metal under pressure into a reusable steel mold and is the only process that replicates the fill dynamics and residual stress of high-pressure die casting (HPDC) production. Investment casting pours metal into a ceramic shell built from a 3D-printed wax pattern, requires no hard tooling, and supports a much broader range of alloys and more complex geometry — but it isn’t a valid stand-in for HPDC-specific production, since die-cast and investment-cast aluminum behave differently. Which casting process is fastest and cheapest for low-volume prototypes? Investment casting is typically the fastest and lowest-cost option for low-volume metal prototypes, since 3D-printed wax patterns eliminate the need for hard tooling and first parts can arrive in 1 to 3 weeks. It’s best suited for runs of roughly 1 to 500 parts; higher volumes shift the cost advantage toward die casting or gravity casting. Can die-cast aluminum prototypes be heat treated to T6? Generally, no. Most HPDC aluminum alloys (such as A380, A383, A360, and ADC12) trap gas during high-pressure mold fill, which can cause surface blistering when the part undergoes the solution phase of T6 heat treatment. Alloys that need T6 heat treatment are usually better suited to gravity/permanent mold casting, where lower-turbulence filling reduces trapped gas. What is gravity casting (permanent mold casting) used for? Gravity (permanent mold) casting pours molten metal into a reusable steel or iron mold using only gravity, rather than injection pressure, which produces less turbulence and trapped gas than die casting. This makes it a common choice for heat-treatable structural aluminum parts, pressure-tight enclosures, and mid-complexity aluminum housings at volumes of roughly 50 to 3,000 parts. How much does tooling cost and lead time vary between casting methods? Investment casting requires no tooling since patterns are 3D-printed, giving it the shortest lead time (1–3 weeks). Gravity/permanent mold casting requires reusable metal tooling with a 3–5 week lead time, while die casting tooling — especially hardened production tooling rather than soft tooling — takes the longest at roughly 2–8 weeks and carries the highest upfront cost. How does prototyping with casting help with the transition to full production? Prototyping with the same casting process family as production means the design, tooling decisions, alloy behavior, and DFM constraints carry forward directly. A die-cast prototype validates fill dynamics and residual stress under conditions comparable to production; an investment-cast prototype confirms alloy behavior and geometry feasibility before production quantities are committed. The closer the prototype process matches production, the fewer engineering changes are required during the production qualification phase — and the more useful the prototype test data is for predicting production part performance.

Be Part of the PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest! by: PCBWay Sep 03,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News We are glad to announce that PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest has arrived. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. Awards and corresponding prizes: The First Prize : 1 winner, $1500 Cash + $200 Coupon + A Palm-sized Robot Dog*1 The Second Prize : 2 winners, $1000 Cash + $100 Coupon + Raspberry Pi 5 4GB *1 The Third Prize : 3 winners, $500 Cash + $50 Coupon + OpenMV4 H7 R2 Cam Smart Camera *1 Popular Design Prize : 10 winners, $100 Cash + $20 Coupon + $10 3D Printing Coupon + Multimeter ZTY890DPro *1 Participation Prize : Raspberry Pi Pico * 1 STM32 Great Project Prize : Six-Claw Multifunctional Aluminum Alloy Soldering Table *1 For more detailed information about the contest, please refer to: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . If there are any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below.We wish you the best of luck and look forward to your innovative designs! Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Employees must be provided with fair compensation and reasonable rest periods, and their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining must be respected. Business Ethics and Compliance Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting any form of bribery is strictly prohibited; effective conflict of interest management and whistleblowing mechanisms must be in place. All financial and business records must accurately, completely, and truthfully reflect the underlying transactions. Full compliance with international sanctions, export controls, and other applicable laws and regulations is required. Supply Chain Responsibility and Sustainable Procurement PCBWay and its partners are required to extend the principles outlined in this document to all levels of entities within the supply chain. Priority should be given to selecting partners that are legally compliant, socially responsible, and committed to sustainable development. Identify social, labor, and environmental risks related to operations, and develop corresponding control and mitigation measures. Encourage partners to prioritize local sourcing to support regional economic development and job creation. Environmental Protection and Workplace Safety Actively implement environmental protection measures and continuously promote energy conservation and emission reduction; Ensure that all waste and hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The procurement or use of prohibited materials is not allowed. Provide employees with a safe working environment and health support mechanisms to prevent occupational injuries and health risks. PCBWay has fully adopted the DHL GoGreen transportation service in 2025 to reduce carbon emissions in the supply chain and promote the development of a green supply chain, with an initial target of reducing emissions by 30%. Information Protection and Transparent Governance Establish a comprehensive security system to strictly protect the confidentiality of customer data, drawings, and other business information. Comply with relevant laws and regulations to safeguard the personal data of customers and employees. Ensure that financial records are true, accurate, and complete, and prohibit any illegal activities. PCBWay will ensure the implementation of the above principles in actual cooperation and reserves the right to take action against any violations. Verify Now Blog > Impact of the New U.S. Tariff Policy on Customs Clearance Impact of the New U.S. Tariff Policy on Customs Clearance by: PCBWay Feb 05,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Summary： US imposes new tariffs on Chinese products Update on Dec 31th Current Tax Rates for Various PCBWay Products Bare PCBs : 45% Assembled boards : 35% Steel 、Aluminum& Copper (CNC,stencil, etc.) : About 85% SMT printing stencil :88% Others: General duty rates plus 10% Note: The above tax rates are estimated for reference only, as tax rates are subject to significant real-time fluctuations. NOTE: CBP has provided this chart as a courtesy for informational purposes only, and it does not constitute an official interpretation of the application of tariffs by CBP or the U.S. government. The language of each individual Executive Order and Proclamation, as well as applicable Federal Register Notices, are dispositive as to the application of tariffs to imported products. Importers are responsible for exercising reasonable care in calculating applicable tariffs to their products based on all applicable legal authorities and correctly declaring the amount to CBP on entry documentation. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Update on June 24th Current Tax Rates for Various PCBWay Products Bare PCBs : 55% Stencils : 98% SMT Services : 45% CNC Machining : 65% Aluminum & Steel Components : 73% Plastic Components : 65% Other Products : 55% Note: The above tax rates are estimated for reference only, as tax rates are subject to significant real-time fluctuations. News Update： Updated on May 8th Updated on May 15th Note: The current official Fedex website's charging standard still takes 800 as the dividing line. The dividing line between formal and informal customs declaration is 2500 In response to recent changes, we currently recommends the following logistics options: We advise using DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) logistics services with prepaid tariffs, such as: 1. DHL DTP (Duty & Tax Prepaid) , SF express If the item falls under HTS codes 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 10% tariff exemption. However, DHL may incorrectly apply duties. If the recipient is charged duties despite the exemption, dispute it with DHL immediately—delays may invalidate the claim. DHL DTP will prepay customs duties & taxes. DHL may contact recipients for required documentation/clarification to clear shipments (regardless of Incoterm® used). Download POA form: [POA form.pdf] Due to tariff uncertainty, we will apply a 30%~73%duty rate (current U.S. rates: 30%~73%%, with a 10% exemption for 9903.01.32/33). When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. (3) Effective June 1, 2025 at 12:01 AM EST: The flat tariff will increase to $200 $150 per item. 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33 , the tariff exemption is 125% ) 104% Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** For Chinese-origin goods valued over $800: Effective April 9, 2025 at 12:01 AM EST: An additional tariff of 125% 104% will be applied to these products. 3.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. 4.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. Note: All times mentioned are in U.S. Eastern Standard Time (EST). Regarding the latest US tariff policy, PCBWay will temporarily maintain the DDP/DTP charges unchanged. https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/amendment-to-recipricol-tariffs-and-updated-duties-as-applied-to-low-value-imports-from-the-peoples-republic-of-china/ Expected situation: If the category is under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the equivalent tariff is exempted by 125%： 20% (fentanyl) +25% (if 232 surcharges are involved) +25% (if 301 surcharges are involved) + exemption from equivalent tariffs + most-favored-nation rates ranging from 0% to 6.5%, with some combined rates reaching 45% to 76.5% Other: 20% (fentanyl) +125% equivalent tariff +25% (if 301 surcharge is involved) + most-favored-nation rates ranging from 0 to 6.5%, with some combined rates reaching 145% to 176.5% Note: 8471 is under the U.S. HS exemption code of 9903.01.32 and is not related to Section 232. The exemption scope of 9903.01.32 includes semiconductors, as well as some goods listed by the United States within the HS list. The applicable exemption scope of 9903.01.33 includes automobiles and some parts and components, and it is related to the Section 232 list. 9903.01.63 refers to goods other than those within the scopes of 9903.01.32 and 9903.01.33, and an additional 125% tariff will be imposed on them. =============================================================================================================================================== How Much Are Tariffs on Chinese Goods? It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The new 125 percent rate that President Trump imposed will in many cases be added on top of long-existing duties. There are four main categories of tariffs that are imposed on goods from China. Note: The tariff on auto parts comes into effect in early May. The average provided for the base rate is calculated by the World Trade Organization, which computes an average of all tariff lines. A large share of U.S. imports are assigned a 0% duty, but there are some very high rates in the tariff schedule. Rates ultimately depend on what is imported, what materials are used (from where), which special rates are applied and what sorts of products are exempt. New tariff rates on select goods from China Note: Rates are rounded to the nearest whole number. The rates are calculated assuming metal furniture made of 100 percent aluminum and door hinges made of 50 percent aluminum. Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Note: If you want to place an assembly order, please be sure to add MPN information to the BOM. This can help the quoter source the devices you need more accurately. Manual installation Except for the way mentioned before, you can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Fabrication-Toolkit-for-KiCad: Open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About BOM Through BOM files, we can get all information of the components used in your design. In order to speed up the quotation process, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) If you have more suggestions, please leave a message below, PCBWay has committed to providing everyone with high-quality services. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for ProtoFlow PCBWay Plug-In for ProtoFlow by: PCBWay Oct 20,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News ProtoFlow is an AI-assisted PCB design tool for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It brings schematic capture, PCB layout and routing, and manufacturing file exports into one workspace. Users can describe a circuit in plain language to generate an editable schematic, then review, refine, and simulate the design. ProtoFlow also supports importing from and exporting to major EDA tools. Here is the link to ProtoFlow: https://www.protoflow.ai/ We’re excited to announce that PCBWay and ProtoFlow have teamed up to make the journey from PCB design to manufacturing easier. As AI continues to transform the way we work, ProtoFlow brings AI-assisted capabilities to PCB design, helping users design, simulate, and validate their boards before manufacturing. ProtoFlow takes PCBWay’s manufacturing requirements into account during the design process and checks the board for manufacturability before export, helping users identify and address potential issues early. Its built-in simulation tools and AI agent also allow users to test designs against their own requirements and refine them until all checks pass. Once the design is ready, users can send their Gerber, BOM, and coordinate files directly to PCBWay with just one click and go straight to the quotation page. This integration creates a smoother workflow from AI-assisted design to PCB manufacturing, helping makers and engineers turn their ideas into reality with greater ease: Ready to give it a try? Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Store NewArrival Product - M5Stack CoreS3 ESP32S3 IoT Development Kit PCBWay Store NewArrival Product - M5Stack CoreS3 ESP32S3 IoT Development Kit by: PCBWay Oct 08,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCBWay Store Link： CoreS3 CoreS3 is the third-generation main controller of the M5Stack development kit series, based on the ESP32-S3 solution featuring a dual-core Xtensa LX7 processor running at 240 MHz with built-in Wi-Fi. It integrates 16MB Flash and 8MB PSRAM. Programs can be downloaded through the USB Type-C port, and OTG & CDC functions are supported for connecting USB devices and flashing firmware. The front houses a 2.0-inch capacitive-touch IPS panel protected by high-strength glass. Below the screen is a 0.3MP GC0308 camera paired with an LTR-553ALS-WA proximity sensor. Power is managed by an AXP2101 PMU and four power-path control circuits, delivering a low-power design. Onboard sensors include a six-axis IMU BMI270 and a magnetometer BMM150. Additional peripherals comprise a microSD slot and a BM8563 RTC, enabling precise time-keeping plus sleep/timed-wake-up functions. For audio, a 16-bit I2S amplifier AW88298 drives the built-in 1W speaker, while an ES7210 audio codec provides dual-microphone input. Independent POWER and RESET (RST) buttons are located on the side; long-pressing the RESET button enters download mode via a self-built delay circuit. The kit ships with a DinBase for DIN-rail, wall-mount or screw mounting. It can be powered by an external DC 12V (9 ~ 24V) supply or an internal 500mAh Li-ion battery. Multiple proto areas on the DinBase ease DIY expansion. Ideal for IoT development, DIY projects, smart-home control systems and industrial automation control systems. Verify Now Blog > How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements by: Mila Oct 21,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Assembly PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer provides a special assembly service price for eligible PCB prototypes. It is designed for relatively simple projects with limited assembly requirements. Not every PCB assembly project qualifies for this offer. Your project must meet the technical requirements listed below, and the promotion is subject to customer eligibility and usage limits. $29 PCB Assembly Requirements To qualify for the $29 PCB assembly offer, your project must meet all of the following requirements: Component Sourcing: All components must be supplied by PCBWay. PCB Type: Only rigid PCBs are eligible. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are not supported by this offer. Assembly Quantity: No more than 20 boards per order. Components per Board: Each board can have a maximum of 200 components. Total Component Quantity: The total number of components across the order cannot exceed 600. Unique Component Types: The project can include no more than 100 different component types. Through-Hole Solder Joints: The total number of through-hole solder joints cannot exceed 100. All limits are inclusive. For example, an order for exactly 20 boards or a project with exactly 100 different component types can qualify, provided that all other requirements are also met. Important: Meeting these technical requirements does not automatically guarantee the promotional price. Your order must also meet the applicable customer eligibility and monthly usage limits. How Often Can You Use the $29 PCB Assembly Offer? The $29 PCB assembly promotion has a monthly usage limit based on customer status. New customers: Eligible new customers can use the offer once per month. Returning customers: Eligible returning customers can use the offer up to twice per month. If you submit multiple orders at the same time, only one eligible order can receive the $29 promotional price. The remaining orders will be charged at their applicable rates. Please note that each order must meet all the technical requirements to qualify for the promotion. The monthly usage limit does not mean that every order you submit will receive the special price. How to Get $29 PCB Assembly on PCBWay Follow these steps to get started. Step 1: Prepare your PCB design files Prepare your Gerber files, Bill of Materials (BOM), and pick-and-place file, as applicable to your project. Step 2: Check your project requirements Confirm that your project uses rigid PCBs, that all components will be supplied by PCBWay, and that your assembly quantity and component counts are within the specified limits. Step 3: Submit your assembly order Visit the PCBWay PCB Assembly Service page and submit your PCB assembly files and requirements. Step 4: Confirm your eligibility Check your eligibility for the promotion and make sure you have not exceeded the applicable usage limit. The final price is subject to order review and confirmation. Frequently Asked Questions -Can I use the $29 PCB assembly offer for flex PCBs or rigid-flex PCBs? No. The promotion is available for rigid PCBs only. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are excluded. -Can I supply my own components? No. All components must be supplied by PCBWay to qualify for this offer. -Can I order more than 20 boards? No. The maximum eligible assembly quantity is 20 boards per order. -How many components can my PCB have? Each board can have no more than 200 components, and the total component quantity across the order cannot exceed 600. -Is there a limit on component types? Yes. The project can include no more than 100 different component types. -Are through-hole components allowed? Projects with through-hole components may qualify, provided that the total number of through-hole solder joints does not exceed 100 and all other requirements are met. -Can I apply the $29 price to multiple orders submitted at once? No. Only one eligible order can receive the promotional price when multiple orders are submitted together. -Can I use the offer again next month? The promotion may be available again according to the applicable monthly usage limit. Please check your eligibility before placing another order. -Does the $29 price cover my entire PCB project? The $29 offer is a special PCB assembly price, not necessarily the total cost of your project. PCB fabrication, components, shipping, and other applicable charges may be quoted separately. PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer is designed to make simple PCB prototypes more affordable. Check the eligibility requirements before ordering to ensure your project meets the technical limits and promotion rules. Ready to get started? Verify Now Blog > How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements by: Mila Oct 21,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Assembly PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer provides a special assembly service price for eligible PCB prototypes. It is designed for relatively simple projects with limited assembly requirements. Not every PCB assembly project qualifies for this offer. Your project must meet the technical requirements listed below, and the promotion is subject to customer eligibility and usage limits. $29 PCB Assembly Requirements To qualify for the $29 PCB assembly offer, your project must meet all of the following requirements: Component Sourcing: All components must be supplied by PCBWay. PCB Type: Only rigid PCBs are eligible. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are not supported by this offer. Assembly Quantity: No more than 20 boards per order. Components per Board: Each board can have a maximum of 200 components. Total Component Quantity: The total number of components across the order cannot exceed 600. Unique Component Types: The project can include no more than 100 different component types. Through-Hole Solder Joints: The total number of through-hole solder joints cannot exceed 100. All limits are inclusive. For example, an order for exactly 20 boards or a project with exactly 100 different component types can qualify, provided that all other requirements are also met. Important: Meeting these technical requirements does not automatically guarantee the promotional price. Your order must also meet the applicable customer eligibility and monthly usage limits. How Often Can You Use the $29 PCB Assembly Offer? The $29 PCB assembly promotion has a monthly usage limit based on customer status. New customers: Eligible new customers can use the offer once per month. Returning customers: Eligible returning customers can use the offer up to twice per month. If you submit multiple orders at the same time, only one eligible order can receive the $29 promotional price. The remaining orders will be charged at their applicable rates. Please note that each order must meet all the technical requirements to qualify for the promotion. The monthly usage limit does not mean that every order you submit will receive the special price. How to Get $29 PCB Assembly on PCBWay Follow these steps to get started. Step 1: Prepare your PCB design files Prepare your Gerber files, Bill of Materials (BOM), and pick-and-place file, as applicable to your project. Step 2: Check your project requirements Confirm that your project uses rigid PCBs, that all components will be supplied by PCBWay, and that your assembly quantity and component counts are within the specified limits. Step 3: Submit your assembly order Visit the PCBWay PCB Assembly Service page and submit your PCB assembly files and requirements. Step 4: Confirm your eligibility Check your eligibility for the promotion and make sure you have not exceeded the applicable usage limit. The final price is subject to order review and confirmation. Frequently Asked Questions -Can I use the $29 PCB assembly offer for flex PCBs or rigid-flex PCBs? No. The promotion is available for rigid PCBs only. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are excluded. -Can I supply my own components? No. All components must be supplied by PCBWay to qualify for this offer. -Can I order more than 20 boards? No. The maximum eligible assembly quantity is 20 boards per order. -How many components can my PCB have? Each board can have no more than 200 components, and the total component quantity across the order cannot exceed 600. -Is there a limit on component types? Yes. The project can include no more than 100 different component types. -Are through-hole components allowed? Projects with through-hole components may qualify, provided that the total number of through-hole solder joints does not exceed 100 and all other requirements are met. -Can I apply the $29 price to multiple orders submitted at once? No. Only one eligible order can receive the promotional price when multiple orders are submitted together. -Can I use the offer again next month? The promotion may be available again according to the applicable monthly usage limit. Please check your eligibility before placing another order. -Does the $29 price cover my entire PCB project? The $29 offer is a special PCB assembly price, not necessarily the total cost of your project. PCB fabrication, components, shipping, and other applicable charges may be quoted separately. PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer is designed to make simple PCB prototypes more affordable. Check the eligibility requirements before ordering to ensure your project meets the technical limits and promotion rules. Ready to get started? Verify Now Blog > 12 PCB Layout Guidelines for Better Component Placement 12 PCB Layout Guidelines for Better Component Placement by: Mila Oct 29,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout PCB Layout PCB Component Placement PCB Layout Guidelines PCB Design Guidelines PCB layout involves more than simply placing components and routing traces. Component spacing, decoupling capacitor placement, pad connections, thermal management, and manufacturing constraints all affect PCB assembly quality and long-term reliability. The following PCB layout guidelines cover 12 practical details that engineers should consider during PCB component placement and design. 1. SMT Component Spacing The spacing between surface-mount technology (SMT) components is an important consideration in PCB layout. Insufficient spacing can make solder paste printing and component placement more difficult, increase the risk of solder bridging, and complicate rework and maintenance. The following values can serve as preliminary references for PCB component spacing: Same-type components: A spacing of at least 0.3 mm may be used as a reference. Different types of components: A spacing of at least 0.13 × h + 0.3 mm may be used as a reference, where h is the maximum height difference between adjacent components. Components requiring manual placement or rework: A spacing of at least 1.5 mm may be considered, depending on the available working space and tools. These values are for reference only and are not universal manufacturing standards. Actual PCB component spacing should be determined based on component packages, pad dimensions, solder paste printing, placement equipment, and the manufacturing and assembly capabilities of the PCB supplier. 2. Spacing Between Through-Hole and SMT Components Adequate spacing should also be maintained between through-hole components and SMT components to prevent interference during component placement, soldering, and subsequent rework. A spacing of 1–3 mm can serve as a general reference, but the actual distance depends on component dimensions, lead positions, soldering methods, and maintenance requirements. For PCBs assembled using wave soldering, engineers should also consider component orientation, shadowing effects caused by adjacent components, and whether solder can reach the joints effectively. 3. IC Decoupling Capacitor Placement Decoupling capacitors should be placed as close as practical to the corresponding IC power pins. This helps shorten the current loop between the power supply and ground, reducing parasitic inductance and power supply noise. When an IC has multiple power pins, the number, capacitance, and placement of decoupling capacitors should be determined according to the datasheet, power distribution network, and actual current requirements. Where individual power pins require dedicated decoupling, the corresponding capacitors should be placed as close to those pins as possible. The grounding path is equally important. Keep the connections between the power pin, decoupling capacitor, and ground as short as practical. Unnecessarily long traces or excessive vias can reduce decoupling effectiveness, particularly at high frequencies. 4. Component Orientation and Clearance Near PCB Edges PCBs often undergo routing, V-scoring, or other depanelization processes. Components near PCB edges therefore require special attention to their orientation and clearance. First, consider the mechanical stress generated during depanelization. Ceramic capacitors, connectors, and other mechanically sensitive components should be positioned to minimize stress concentration at solder joints and component bodies. Component orientation should be determined by the depanelization method, pad geometry, and component characteristics rather than by a universal rule that all components must be parallel to the cutting direction. Second, sufficient component-free space should be maintained near PCB edges to prevent damage from cutting tools or depanelization equipment. The required clearance depends on the depanelization method, such as V-scoring, routing, or mouse bites, as well as component dimensions and the PCB manufacturer's capabilities. For components that are particularly sensitive to mechanical stress, consider using a depanelization method that reduces stress on the board and solder joints. 5. Connecting Adjacent PCB Pads When adjacent pads must be connected to the same net, the copper connections and trace widths should be planned carefully. Poorly designed copper connections may reduce the effective clearance between pads and increase the risk of solder bridging. During PCB layout, maintain adequate electrical clearance between pads and select trace widths according to current-carrying requirements. For fine-pitch components, pay particular attention to the relationship between pads, traces, and solder mask openings to avoid problems with solder paste printing and soldering quality. After completing the layout, run design rule checks (DRC) and verify that the design meets the PCB manufacturer's fabrication and assembly requirements. 6. Thermal Relief vs. Solid Copper Connections When a pad is connected to a copper plane, the connection method should be selected based on soldering requirements, current-carrying capacity, and thermal performance. Two common methods are thermal relief connections and solid copper connections. A thermal relief connection uses several narrow copper spokes to connect the pad to the surrounding copper plane. This reduces heat transfer from the pad into the larger copper area during soldering, making soldering and rework easier in many cases. A solid copper connection directly connects the pad to the copper plane. It generally provides lower electrical and thermal resistance, but the larger copper area can draw heat away from the pad, making it more difficult to reach the required soldering temperature. The appropriate method depends on current requirements, heat dissipation, soldering processes, and rework needs. For high-current or thermally demanding connections, do not reduce the number or width of copper spokes solely to make soldering easier without evaluating the electrical and thermal consequences. 7. Using Teardrops in PCB Layout When a trace connects to a pad or via through a narrow junction, a teardrop can be added where appropriate to create a smoother transition between the trace and the connection point. Teardrops offer several potential benefits: Improved connection reliability: They increase the copper area at the trace-to-pad junction, helping reduce the risk of a weakened or broken connection caused by drill misalignment, manufacturing tolerances, or mechanical stress. Enhanced mechanical robustness: The wider transition can make the connection less vulnerable to local narrowing or separation. Improved appearance: Teardrops create a smoother visual transition between traces and pads. However, teardrops are not necessary in every situation. For high-speed or impedance-sensitive traces, engineers should evaluate whether the resulting geometric changes could affect impedance continuity or signal integrity. 8. Trace Width at Component Pads During PCB layout, trace widths near component pads should be selected according to the electrical and mechanical requirements of the design. For differential signals, symmetrical analog circuits, and connections requiring balanced current distribution, trace symmetry, width matching, and length matching may be important for maintaining signal integrity and circuit performance. However, ordinary signal traces do not always need to have identical widths on both sides of a pad. Trace widths should be determined by current-carrying capacity, impedance requirements, pad dimensions, and manufacturing capabilities. Avoid unnecessary abrupt changes in trace width near pad connections. 9. Handling Unused IC Pins Unused IC pins must be handled according to the device datasheet and application requirements. They should not all be connected to ground or left floating indiscriminately. For example: NC pins: Follow the datasheet instructions. Some pins must remain unconnected and should not be grounded without authorization. Unused input pins: Connect them to the specified logic level or use the recommended pull-up, pull-down, or other biasing method to prevent undefined input states. Unused output pins: Do not connect them directly to ground or a power rail unless the datasheet explicitly permits it. Pins permitted to float: Leave them unconnected only when this is allowed or required by the device documentation. For physical pins that are present on the IC but not used in the application, ensure that the PCB footprint correctly represents the actual package. Whether the corresponding pads should be connected to ground or handled in another way depends on the pin function and the device manufacturer's recommendations. Adding a pad and connecting it to ground does not necessarily provide effective shielding. An incorrect connection may instead cause a short circuit or interfere with normal device operation. 10. Via-in-Pad Design Considerations During PCB layout, placing a conventional open via directly within a pad can cause solder to flow into the hole during assembly. This may result in insufficient solder at the joint, poor soldering quality, or other assembly defects. For ordinary SMT pads, avoid placing untreated open vias directly within the pads, particularly for fine-pitch components, unless the manufacturing process supports the design. However, vias are not universally prohibited within pads. Via-in-pad is a common design approach for packages such as BGAs, where routing density and electrical performance may require it. Depending on the application, via filling, capping, or other appropriate via treatments may be needed to prevent solder loss and ensure reliable assembly. Select the appropriate approach based on the component package, via structure, and PCB manufacturer's process capabilities. 11. PCB Edge Clearance for Traces, Pads, and Components Copper traces, pads, and components should maintain adequate clearance from PCB edges to prevent damage during fabrication, depanelization, and subsequent assembly. If copper features or pads are too close to the board edge, routing, V-scoring, or other depanelization processes may damage the copper, expose conductors, or compromise electrical reliability. For single-sided boards and substrates with relatively low mechanical strength, additional attention should be paid to structural integrity and component placement near the edges. The required PCB edge clearance should be determined according to the board material, thickness, depanelization method, and manufacturer's capabilities. Include these clearances in the PCB design rules and verify them before manufacturing. 12. Keep Electrolytic Capacitors Away from Heat Sources Electrolytic capacitors are sensitive to operating temperature. Prolonged exposure to elevated temperatures can accelerate electrolyte loss and shorten capacitor service life. During PCB layout, avoid placing electrolytic capacitors too close to power resistors, power semiconductors, transformers, or other heat-generating components whenever possible. If close placement is unavoidable, evaluate the thermal impact based on component temperature rise, airflow direction, and the actual operating environment. Also consider the capacitor's rated operating temperature, ripple current, and self-heating to ensure that it operates within acceptable limits under real-world conditions. Distance from a heat source alone is not sufficient to determine whether a capacitor is safe. Thermal design and the operating conditions of the complete product must also be considered. Conclusion PCB layout affects not only electrical performance but also manufacturability, soldering quality, and long-term reliability. In addition to routing and component placement, engineers should consider assembly processes, mechanical stress, thermal requirements, and the recommendations provided in component datasheets. After completing the PCB design, perform design rule checks and verify the layout against the PCB manufacturer's capabilities and assembly requirements. Careful attention to these PCB layout guidelines can help reduce design issues and improve PCB fabrication and assembly reliability Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac.
